buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Terms and Conditions for Allied Civil Works 1. Scope of Work 1.1 The scope of allied civil works includes, but is not limited to: * Brickwork & Masonry: Construction of brick walls, partitions, and structural supports using specified first-class bricks and standard mortar mix (1:4 or 1:6 as specified). * MS Shed Structure: Fabrication, supply, anti-corrosive priming, double-coat painting, and erection of Mil d Steel (MS) shed structures along with suitable roofing sheets. * Platforms & Foundations: Construction of reinforced concrete/brickwork platforms to house heavy securi ty hardware, racks, generators, or control panels. * Doors & Windows: Supply and installation of heavy-duty MS/aluminium/UPVC doors and windows with su itable locking mechanisms, wire mesh (where required), and weatherproofing. * Flooring Works: Provision of durable flooring (tiled, IPS, anti-static, or epoxy coating as specified for cont rol/equipment rooms). * False Ceiling & Wall Panelling: Installation of acoustic/modular false ceilings and wall panelling suitable f

or concealing cables and enhancing control room thermal/acoustic insulation. * Electrical Lighting & Power Outlets: Installation of internal fixtures, LED lighting panels, conduits, wiring, MCBs, DBs, and earthing required to illuminate and power the room/shed prior to equipment commissionin g. * Integration & Finishing: Surface finishing, plastering, painting, cable trenching/conduiting, and complete cleanup to make the site ready for equipment installation. 2. Quality of Materials & Standard Specifications 2.1 All materials supplied by the contractor (cement, steel, bricks, paint, wiring, ceiling tiles, etc.) shall con form to the relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) or equivalent codes. 2.2 MS Work: Steel sections must be free from rust, scales, or defects. All joints must be fully welded and ground smooth before applying one coat of red oxide primer and two coats of approved synthetic enamel paint. 2.3 Brickwork & Plastering: Bricks must be well-burnt, uniform in shape, and cured properly for a minimum of 7 days. Plastering shall have a smooth finish ready for paint/panelling. 2.4 False Ceiling & Panelling: Framework for false ceilings and wall panelling must be securely anchored to structural walls/slabs with non-corrosive hardware. Materials must be fire-retardant where specified for se curity control rooms. 3. Site Inspection, Layout, and Approvals 3.1 The contractor shall perform a detailed joint site survey with the Client/Engineer-in-Charge before com mencing work. 3.2 All dimensions, structural levels, cable entry points, cutouts for security equipment, and door/window s wings must be verified against approved layout drawings. 3.3 Any deviation from the approved drawings must receive written authorization from the Engineer-in-Ch arge prior to execution. 4. Co-ordination with Security Equipment Suppliers/Integrators 4.1 The civil contractor shall work in close coordination with the security equipment installation agency to ensure exact positioning of foundations, wall openings, conduit entries, and mounting brackets. 4.2 Trenching, floor ducting, and conduit embedment must be completed strictly in accordance with the c able routing plan provided by the security integrator. 5. Workmanship, Testing, and Commissioning 5.1 Workmanship: Execution must meet high engineering standards. Poor finish, misaligned panels, saggin g false ceilings, or uneven flooring will lead to rejection of work. 5.2 Electrical Testing: Lighting circuits, distribution boards, and earthing provisions must be tested for cont inuity, insulation resistance, and proper grounding before handing over the room/shed. 5.3 Completion & Handover: Civil works shall be deemed complete only after joint inspection and issuance of a Completion Certificate by the designated Engineer-in-Charge. 6. Defect Liability Period (DLP) 6.1 The Contractor shall guarantee all civil, structural, electrical lighting, and finishing works against defec ts for a period of 12 months from the date of final commissioning and handover. 6.2 Any defects such as roof leaks, plaster cracks, paint peeling, structural sagging, loose paneling, or elec trical fitting failures arising within the DLP shall be rectified by the contractor at their own cost within 48 to 72 hours of notice. 7. Safety, Site Security, and Debris Disposal 7.1 The contractor must comply with all applicable safety standards, providing necessary Personal Protecti ve Equipment (PPE) to all workers on site. 7.2 Since the work is within/around a security zone, all contractor personnel must undergo security verifica tion and adhere to access control protocols dictated by the facility owner. 7.3 The site must be maintained clean during execution. All construction debris, leftover steel cuts, mortar residue, and packaging must be cleared and disposed of at approved locations before final handover. .
